title: Rental contracts that renew automatically
detail: Standard rental contracts that renew automatically (*prórroga automática*), so tenants and small landlords have stability. The programme gives no length or conditions.
c: Automatic renewal already exists (5 to 7 years under the 2019 law). Making it longer is realistic by ordinary law, but the programme gives no details.
pos: Stability for tenants: fewer moves and fewer big rent rises when contracts renew.
neg: Landlords have less freedom and may stop renting long-term.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 7/2019 on rentals: contracts extended to 5–7 years (BOE)

title: Ban buying homes to make a profit
detail: Ban companies, investment funds and large owners from buying homes. Large foreign buyers would need to be on the local register (*padrón*) for at least 2 years, and use the home as their main home or rent it at a controlled price. Whole buildings could be bought only for rental at controlled prices.
c: A general ban on companies buying homes goes against arts. 33 and 38 of the Constitution and the EU rule on free movement of money.

title: Limit yearly rent rises to 2%
detail: A permanent 2% limit on yearly rent rises whenever yearly inflation (*IPC*) is higher. Landlords who raise the rent above the last contract or the index limit would lose their tax deductions.
c: A 2 to 3% limit on yearly rises already applied from 2022 to 2024. A permanent limit changes agreed contracts, and when inflation is high, owners would leave the rental market.
pos: It protects tenants when prices rise fast, as the 2022 to 2024 limit did.
neg: A permanent limit below inflation lowers what landlords really earn, so they may sell or move to short-term rentals.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 6/2022: 2% cap on rent updates (BOE)
Ley 12/2023 on the right to housing (BOE)

title: Act against illegal tourist flats
detail: Present again the bill that stops platforms from advertising and booking illegal tourist flats (*vivienda turística*). Congress accepted it for debate, but then it stopped moving. 21% VAT on short tourist rentals, and state money for towns with stressed areas.
c: A ban on advertising illegal flats fits the 2024 EU rules on short-term rentals, and it is realistic.
pos: Fewer illegal tourist flats and more homes for people who live there.
neg: Platforms will challenge it under EU law. A ban on ads also hits small owners who are still waiting for a licence.

s.t: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 on short-term rental data (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Bring back the special tax on energy companies; tax banks and large fortunes
detail: Bring back the special tax on energy companies (*gravamen energético*) and make it permanent. PNV, PP, Vox, UPN and Junts voted against it. The Basque and Navarre tax offices (*Haciendas Forales*) would collect it. Raise taxes on banks and large fortunes. No amounts are given.
c: Congress did not approve the energy tax in January 2025 (165 for, 183 against). It cannot pass again without votes from the right and some nationalist parties.
pos: More tax money from companies with unusually high profits and from rich people.
neg: A tax on energy companies may mean they invest less in grids and renewable energy. Banks pass their tax on to customers.

s.t: BOE, 23 Jan 2025: Congress did not approve RDL 10/2024 on the energy levy

title: A 32-hour week with the same pay
detail: Cut working time to 32 hours a week, or four working days, with no loss of pay, by changing the Workers' Statute (*Estatuto de los Trabajadores*). Small and medium businesses would start at 35 hours and reach the goal within three years.
c: As with Sumar and Podemos: even 37.5 hours did not pass in 2025.

s.t: Congress, BOCG 15-A-58-3: 37.5-hour bill returned to the government (10 Sep 2025)

title: Regularisation and a new immigration law
detail: A regularisation (*regularización*) that works, is easy to use and lasts. It would give residence and work permits and stop people from losing their legal status again. A new immigration law based on human rights. No dates, conditions or numbers are given.
c: As with Sumar, a permanent regularisation needs an organic law, and PP and Vox are against it.
pos: Fewer people work without contracts, so the state gets more tax and social security payments.
neg: A permanent route may attract more people to come (experts disagree on how many). It also puts a lot of pressure on offices, as in the 2026 regularisation (1.17 million applications).

s.t: La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026: 1,174,978 regularisation applications filed
